title: Anaphylaxis in a child
stem: Paediatric resus. A 7-year-old girl (about 23 kg) ate a biscuit at a birthday party 15 minutes ago. She has a swollen face, a hoarse voice, wheeze and hives. HR 150, BP 72/40, RR 36, SpO2 91%. Her aunt is with her.

review.text: Antihistamine and steroid. Your notes still give IM/IV hydrocortisone and chlorphenamine as routine. RCUK (2021) removed both from emergency treatment: an oral non-sedating antihistamine for skin symptoms once stable, and steroids only for refractory reactions or ongoing asthma or shock.

Adrenaline strength. Your notes give '0.1 mL of 1:10,000' as an IM equivalent. 1:10,000 (0.1 mg/mL) is for IV use only; IM adrenaline is always 1:1000 (1 mg/mL). Mixing them up is a known cause of harm.

notes:
Checked against the Resuscitation Council UK emergency treatment of anaphylaxis (2021, with the 2024 update on refractory anaphylaxis) and the RCUK 2025 guidelines.

IM adrenaline 1:1000 (1 mg/mL) into the anterolateral thigh: under 6 months 100–150 microgram; 6 months–6 years 150 microgram; 6–12 years 300 microgram; over 12 years 500 microgram (300 microgram if small or prepubertal). Repeat after 5 minutes if not improving. After 2 IM doses with ongoing respiratory or circulatory problems: refractory anaphylaxis — low-dose IV adrenaline infusion with expert help, and fluids (10 mL/kg crystalloid in children).

Antihistamines and steroids are no longer part of emergency treatment (RCUK 2021): non-sedating oral antihistamine for skin symptoms after stabilisation; steroids only for refractory reactions or ongoing asthma/shock. Your notes still list IM/IV hydrocortisone and chlorphenamine doses as routine; they are not scored here.

Your notes also give the IM dose as '0.1 mL of 1:10,000' as an equivalent: 1:10,000 (0.1 mg/mL) is for IV use only. IM adrenaline must be 1:1000; mixing them up is a known cause of harm.

Mast cell tryptase: first sample as soon as possible after treatment, second within 1–2 hours (no later than 4), third at 24 hours or at follow-up. Observe (6–12 hours depending on severity), discharge with two adrenaline auto-injectors, training and an allergy clinic referral.

steps.label: Assess
steps.hint: Airway, breathing, circulation problems with skin changes after a trigger: anaphylaxis.

ABC.r: Lip and tongue swelling, hoarse voice, soft stridor.

steps.label: Treat
steps.hint: Call for help, lie her down (sit if breathless), IM adrenaline 300 microgram, oxygen, repeat at 5 minutes, fluids.

opts.t: Call for help; remove the trigger
Lie her flat with legs raised (or sitting up if breathing is the problem)
Adrenaline 1:1000, 300 microgram (0.3 mL) IM into the anterolateral thigh
opts.mark: IM adrenaline 300 microgram (6–12 years) into the thigh

opts.t: IV access; crystalloid bolus 10 mL/kg (230 mL)
Not improving at 5 minutes: repeat IM adrenaline 300 microgram

opts.r: 1:10,000 is the IV/cardiac arrest strength; the IM dose is 1:1000. This is a tenfold volume error waiting to happen.

opts.t: Chlorphenamine and hydrocortisone before the adrenaline
opts.r: They do not treat airway or circulation problems and delay adrenaline.
IV bolus adrenaline outside cardiac arrest can cause arrhythmias and myocardial infarction.

opts.t: Mast cell tryptase now, again within 1–2 hours
Observe for at least 12 hours (two doses needed); admit
Two adrenaline auto-injectors, training, an allergy action plan and allergy clinic referral
opts.mark: Discharge plan with auto-injectors and referral

opts.t: If still unwell after two IM doses: refractory anaphylaxis — IV adrenaline infusion with critical care
